items.title: Elevenlabs releases two new speech-to-speech models designed for real-time AI conversations
items.summary: Elevenlabs' new Eleven Realtime speech-to-speech models combine speed and accuracy. The v1 Max variant scores 98.8 percent on the Big Bench Audio benchmark with a 0.57-second response time. Elevenlabs says no model on the Artificial Analysis leaderboard is both faster and more accurate. The article Elevenlabs releases two new speech-to-speech models designed for real-time AI conversations appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Deepseek open-sources the inference engine that powers its fastest and cheapest AI model
items.summary: Deepseek is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its fast V4.1-Flash model. The vLLM-based system cuts compute costs and energy use when running AI models. The release adds more pricing pressure on Western providers like OpenAI and Anthropic. The article Deepseek open-sources the inference engine that powers its fastest and cheapest AI model appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Mistral AI launches Voxtral 3, a full voice agent stack that listens, thinks, and talks in real time
items.summary: Mistral AI launched Voxtral 3, a new family of language models built for real-time voice agents. The system combines speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and a voice agent SDK, supports more than 50 languages, and lets agents tap into external tools during live conversations. items.title: Sam Altman reportedly pitched three endgames for AI safety, one involving a single firm melting everyone else's GPUs
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman laid out three paths to safe AI in an internal presentation: an international watchdog modeled after the IAEA, a merger of the major labs into one entity, or a single company so powerful it could shut down everyone else's compute. He called the last option "terrible." The article Sam Altman reportedly pitched three endgames for AI safety, one involving a single firm melting everyone else's GPUs appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 is much better with legacy programming languages such as COBOL and Fortran
items.summary: OpenAI improved its latest models for low-resource programming languages like COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. On the new MultiLangBench, GPT-6 Astra hits an 87.4 percent test pass rate across 20 languages, up from about 38 percent for GPT-5.6 Terra. items.title: Army Cyber Command's ECHOTRIBBLE would turn AI agents into self-spreading cyberweapons
items.summary: The Army Cyber Command is developing AI agents that move through other networks like a computer worm and "neutralize" targets, according to internal documents. The program, codenamed ECHOTRIBBLE, is designed to reach even air-gapped systems with no network connection and run with minimal human oversight. items.title: Cloudflare's Clairic pulls data from documents faster and cheaper than LLMs
items.summary: Cloudflare has released an AI model it says pulls data from documents faster and more cheaply than large language models. The article Cloudflare's Clairic pulls data from documents faster and cheaper than LLMs appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: US bans Deepseek technology across federal civilian agencies
items.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security has banned federal civilian agencies from using AI technology from Chinese lab Deepseek. The article US bans Deepseek technology across federal civilian agencies appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash shows China's AI price race has no floor in sight
items.summary: MiniMax's M3.1 Flash jumps 13 points over its predecessor to 42 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at half the cost. It also hits 73.7 percent on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark for under $0.30 per task, matching Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017 on both performance and price. The article MiniMax M3.1 Flash shows China's AI price race has no floor in sight appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Kling AI drops version 4.0 with stereo audio, multilingual lip sync, and a lighter Flash variant
items.summary: Kling AI has released version 4.0 of its video generator with support for clips up to 30 seconds, ten keyframe images as input, and prompt comprehension expanded to 8,000 tokens. In comparisons with Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5, Kling 4.0 holds its own but doesn't pull ahead, which could be an early sign that the breakneck pace of progress in AI video models is starting to level off.
